drug_class: GLP-1 receptor agonist and related mechanisms

approved_claims.claim_text: WEGOVY is indicated as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with an initial BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater (obesity), or 27 kg/m2 or greater (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbidity.
approved_claims.evidence_standard: Phase 3 STEP trial program (STEP 1-4), 68-week treatment duration
approved_claims.quantitative_threshold: Mean 15% body weight reduction vs 2.4% placebo at Week 68
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: FDA approved this indication language as class-standard. All subsequent obesity approvals have used identical BMI threshold language.

approved_claims.claim_text: ZEPBOUND is indicated as an adjunct to a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adults with an initial BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater (obesity), or 27 kg/m2 or greater (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbidity.
approved_claims.evidence_standard: Phase 3 SURMOUNT trial program, 72-week treatment duration
approved_claims.quantitative_threshold: Mean 22.5% body weight reduction (15 mg dose) vs 2.5% placebo at Week 72
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: Identical indication language to semaglutide. FDA has standardized this language for the obesity indication class.

approved_claims.claim_text: SAXENDA is indicated as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity for chronic weight management in adult patients with an initial body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2 or greater (obese), or 27 kg/m2 or greater (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbidity.
approved_claims.evidence_standard: Phase 3 SCALE trial program, 56-week treatment duration
approved_claims.quantitative_threshold: Mean 8% body weight reduction vs 2.6% placebo at Week 56
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: Original approval establishing the class indication standard.

approved_claims.claim_text: 83.5% of patients treated with semaglutide 2.4 mg achieved at least 5% reduction in body weight at Week 68 compared with 31.5% of placebo-treated patients.
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: FDA requires responder analysis at >=5% and >=10% thresholds per obesity guidance. This is a mandatory element.

approved_claims.claim_text: In SURMOUNT-1, 96% of patients treated with tirzepatide 15 mg achieved at least 5% body weight reduction at Week 72 compared with 28% of placebo-treated patients.

WEGOVY causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors at clinically relevant exposures in both genders of rats and mice. It is unknown whether WEGOVY causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans.
approved_claims.evidence_standard: Class-effect nonclinical finding. Required for all GLP-1 receptor agonists.
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: BOXED WARNING language. Mandatory for all GLP-1 receptor agonists. FDA will not approve without this warning.

approved_claims.claim_text: ZEPBOUND causes dose-dependent and treatment-duration-dependent thyroid C-cell tumors at clinically relevant exposures in both genders of rats and mice. It is unknown whether ZEPBOUND causes thyroid C-cell tumors, including medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), in humans.
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: Identical boxed warning language to semaglutide. Mandatory class-effect warning.

approved_claims.claim_text: The most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5%) in WEGOVY-treated patients were nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain, headache, fatigue, dyspepsia, dizziness, and gastroenteritis.
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: GI adverse reaction profile is class-defining for GLP-1 agonists.

approved_claims.claim_text: The most common adverse reactions (incidence >=5%) in ZEPBOUND-treated patients were nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain, dyspepsia, injection site reactions, fatigue, and hypersensitivity reactions.
approved_claims.regulatory_notes: GI adverse reaction profile broadly consistent with semaglutide.
